item.title: Make the Adversary Spend More: Stateful Deception as a Cost-Exchange Primitive for AI-Era Cyber Defense
item.description:
This research shows that using a persistent state‑based deception system, powered by a local language model, can force attackers to spend more time and resources while keeping defender cost lower. They built an SSH honeypot that keeps each attacker’s view consistent with their past actions and measured a 63 % reduction in defender effort compared to a basic LLM decoy. It is directly relevant to IT infrastructure managers looking to improve cost‑effective deception.

IT Breakdown: If you manage SSH or similar services, integrate a persistent state honeypot: 1) set up Cowrie with a local LLM; 2) configure the LLM to only render state, not store it; 3) monitor and adjust Deception Exchange Rate to keep defender costs under 63 % of a basic decoy.

item.title: PersonaFactory: Stylistic User Prompt Augmentation with Synthetic Persona Bank
item.description:
PersonaFactory builds a pipeline that creates a huge synthetic persona bank and augments training dialogues with user personas to improve style and intent preservation in LLMs. The system produces 740,000 detailed personas and 1.24 million persona‑styled conversations across 85 languages, and shows that these enriched data help models match user style without losing intent. It is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.

IT Breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work

item.title: [News] Euro-Office comes to your desktop with the Nextcloud Office Desktop app
item.description: Nextcloud has released the Euro-Office Desktop app, a free, open‑source office suite that lets users edit Microsoft Office and OpenDocument files offline and in real time, with features such as digital signatures and local font usage. The app integrates with Nextcloud Hub, allowing teams to co‑edit files on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

item.title: [News] OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work
item.description: OpenAI is merging its ChatGPT and Work experiences, introducing a shared usage meter that may cause heavy users to hit limits sooner. The change is rolling out now to a select group of Pro subscribers, with broader deployment planned for December.

item.title: [News] Meta Refused to Share Muse for Testing, UK Financial Watchdog Complains
item.description: Meta declined to share its Muse AI assistant with the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority for joint testing, prompting the regulator to urge stricter consumer protection oversight. This reflects growing scrutiny of AI assistants that can autonomously make payments or influence consumer behavior.

item.title: [News] MCP servers can now deliver AI agent skills, changing what companies approve when they connect one
item.description: Anthropic has introduced Skills support over the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Claude and Claude Code, now in public beta. This allows AI agents to access external services via MCP, expanding the capabilities of Claude models.

item.title: [News] Introducing the llama.cpp benchmark dashboard for AMD Ryzen and Radeon
item.description: Hugging Face has released a benchmark dashboard that tracks llama.cpp inference performance on AMD Ryzen and Radeon GPUs, allowing users to compare different models, builds, and quantizations. The public data can be used to evaluate and optimize local AI workloads on AMD hardware.
